JNJ.rationale: JNJ is extremely unattractive on all three pillars. Pillar 1 (fundamentals): The company is priced at peak multiples while normalized earnings are deteriorating. Q4 operating margin compressed to 24.9% from 31.2% in Q3, operating cash flow collapsed 72.6% QoQ to $2.51B, and sequential revenue growth has decelerated to +0.3%. The Q1 2025 EPS outlier ($4.54 vs ~$2.14-2.29 in subsequent quarters) inflates TTM metrics; normalized annual EPS is ~$8.56-8.72, not the reported figure. Stelara biosimilar erosion (-41.3% in FY2025) remains a material headwind not yet fully offset. Pillar 2 (valuation): PE of 26.93x sits at the absolute ceiling of the 12-month range (16.6-26.9x), representing a 59% re-rating from 16.96x one year ago — this occurred while margins and ROE (0.317→0.259) are declining, not expanding. P/B of 6.98x is near its ceiling. The 3.7% earnings yield sits 87bps below the 10Y Treasury yield of 4.57%, inverting the historical defensive-valuation relationship. Mean reversion in the PE from 26.9x to the 12-month median of ~19.7x implies ~27% downside absent earnings growth. Pillar 3 (catalyst): The Q1 2025 one-time gain will roll out of the TTM window in the next filing, mechanically inflating reported PE further if price holds — this is a near-term de-rating catalyst, not a positive one. The VIX decline to 16.76 suggests the defensive bid is fading. All three pillars align to the downside.
